question: What is the primary purpose of the community health planning cycle?

options.A: To replace traditional healers with orthodox medical practitioners
options.B: To punish communities that fail to follow sanitation guidelines
options.C: To systematically address population health problems using available resources
options.D: To increase the patient admission rates in tertiary hospitals

explanation: The planning cycle provides a structured framework for public health nurses to tackle community-wide health issues efficiently. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h1)

question: Why is the community health planning cycle described as continuous and circular?

options.A: The exact same health problem must be treated over and over again
options.B: Evaluation findings lead directly into the next round of assessment and planning
options.C: It must be repeated every thirty days regardless of community needs
options.D: Healthcare workers rotate through different villages in a fixed circle

explanation: Because health needs change and programs must adapt, the end of one evaluation simply sparks the beginning of the next planning phase. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h1)

question: Reviewing existing clinic registers and local government health reports is an example of which data collection method?
explanation: Using already recorded data from registers and reports is classed as secondary data because it was collected by someone else previously. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h2)

question: A community health nurse wants to know the exact immunization coverage in a rural village. Which action represents primary data collection?

options.A: Conducting a house-to-house survey to ask mothers about their children's cards
options.B: Checking the national health policy manual for standard vaccination schedules
options.C: Asking the zonal medical officer for the regional vaccination statistics
options.D: Reading the total immunization figures written in the 2021 annual LGA report

explanation: Going directly to the households to gather fresh information from the residents is primary data collection. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h2)

question: Why is priority setting necessary during community health planning?

options.A: Villagers usually refuse to discuss more than a single topic per meeting
options.B: Diseases always occur in isolation rather than in groups
options.C: Government regulations forbid treating more than one disease at a time
options.D: Resources are limited and not all health problems can be solved at once

explanation: Since funds, staff, and time are always limited, nurses must rank problems to tackle the most urgent ones first. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of using a problem tree analysis in community health?

options.A: To map out the geographical boundaries of a farming community
options.B: To measure the exact height and weight of growing children
options.C: To trace visible symptoms back to their underlying root causes
options.D: To calculate the total financial cost of buying medical drugs

explanation: A problem tree helps health workers look past surface symptoms to find the true core cause of a health issue. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h3)

question: What does the letter 'M' stand for in the SMART criteria for objective formulation?
explanation: In SMART planning, objectives must be measurable so the team can prove whether they achieved them or not. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h4)

question: Which of the following is a well-formulated SMART objective for a community health project?

options.A: To improve the general lifestyle and happiness of all market women
options.B: To train 40 traditional birth attendants in safe delivery practices within three months
options.C: To make sure nobody in the entire state ever gets sick with cholera again
options.D: To talk to people about sanitation whenever nurses have free time

explanation: This statement is specific, has a clear number, and includes a strict timeframe, making it truly SMART. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h4)

question: What does resource mobilization in community health primarily involve?

options.A: Storing excess clinic drugs in a locked warehouse for emergencies
options.B: Gathering funds, supplies, transport, and personnel needed for the plan
options.C: Waiting for the federal government to supply all necessary equipment
options.D: Asking international donors to handle every single community project

explanation: Resource mobilization is the active process of securing all types of inputs—human, material, and financial—to execute a health intervention. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h5)

question: Why is it important to involve local community assets during resource mobilization?

options.A: Government policy forbids spending money on outside contractors
options.B: Local villagers are the only people legally allowed to handle medical drugs
options.C: It eliminates the need for nurses to write any project reports
options.D: It builds local ownership and reduces complete reliance on external funding

explanation: Using local resources ensures the community values the project and can sustain it even if external donors leave. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h5)

question: What is the primary activity that takes place during the implementation phase of the health planning cycle?

options.A: Choosing which disease is the most important to study next year
options.B: Writing the initial grant proposal to submit to local government authorities
options.C: Conducting the final research report to present at a university seminar
options.D: Carrying out the planned health activities and delivering services

explanation: Implementation is where the actual work happens, turning plans and strategies into direct health services for the population. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h6)

question: What is a common consequence of poor communication during the implementation phase?

options.A: Immediate dismissal of the local village traditional ruler
options.B: Low community turnout and poor participation in health activities
options.C: A sudden surplus of expired medical vaccines
options.D: Instant failure of government financial auditing systems

explanation: If people do not know when or where a health outreach is happening, they cannot attend, resulting in low turnout. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h6)

question: What is the key difference between monitoring and evaluation?

options.A: Monitoring is done only by doctors, while evaluation is done strictly by patients
options.B: Monitoring happens after the project closes, while evaluation happens before it starts
options.C: Monitoring looks at financial costs, whereas evaluation only looks at weather patterns
options.D: Monitoring is ongoing during the project, while evaluation is a formal assessment of results

explanation: Monitoring is continuous tracking to keep things on track, while evaluation measures the final outcomes and impact. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h7)

question: A community health nurse checks the weekly antenatal clinic register every Friday to ensure attendance numbers are steady. What type of activity is this?
explanation: Reviewing registers weekly during the project to track progress is ongoing monitoring. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge faced in community health planning in Nigeria?

options.A: Cultural resistance and rumors regarding certain public health programs
options.B: Excessive availability of surplus financial funds in primary health centers
options.C: Poor transportation infrastructure in remote rural or riverine areas
options.D: Inadequate funding and delayed budgetary releases from government

explanation: Primary health centers in Nigeria typically suffer from chronic underfunding rather than having excessive surplus funds. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h8)

question: Why is the involvement of traditional and religious leaders crucial when planning community health interventions?

options.A: They are legally required to sign every nurse's monthly salary voucher
options.B: They provide international grants for buying hospital equipment
options.C: They help build trust and dismantle cultural resistance among community members
options.D: They possess formal training in advanced surgical procedures

explanation: Traditional and religious leaders hold massive influence over local beliefs and behavior, making them key allies in overcoming health rumors. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h8)
